What is visible: Mostly dense, leafy green potted oregano held indoors; a few long trailing stems with wider leaf spacing (mild, limited legginess) and some dead-looking material at the base; no pests or disease visible.
Verdict rationale: A brighter, cool spot is sensible for a potted oregano in a UK October and fits the mild legginess, though the plant is otherwise in good shape so it is not urgent.
Quoted issue line(s): "trim the leggy, woody stems to encourage bushier growth"; "Dies back further and rests through winter"
Issue explanation: Trimming for bushier growth now clashes with the app's own note that the plant dies back and rests until March-April; only a light tidy of the longest stems and dead base material suits October.
Recommended first step: Keep it in a bright, cool, free-draining spot, water sparingly, remove the dead basal material and long straggly tips, and leave the main cut-back until spring.

What is visible: Young mint with healthy leaves and one black insect (likely a bug nymph) on a leaf; no visible damage.
App first-action headline: Keep it away from your other plants.
Verdict rationale: Isolating is harmless but excessive for a single insect with no damage in the photo.
Quoted issue line(s): "Don't Water it - Worse than leaving it."
Issue explanation: A blanket no-watering rule is unsupported by the photo; mint likes moist soil and pots under cover can dry out, so it should depend on how wet the compost feels.
Recommended first step: Identify the insect and flick it off if it is a pest, then check leaf undersides; water only if the top of the compost is dry.

What is visible: Pale yellow-green leaves throughout, a few brown patches, flower spikes, pot on a blue plastic tray on a balcony; standing water in the tray is not visible.
Verdict rationale: Removing flower spikes is sound basil practice, but it ignores the main problem of widespread yellowing and the cold exposure of an outdoor basil in mid-October.
Issue explanation: In mid-October a stressed outdoor basil is near the end of its season, so cutting does little; the confidence rating is overstated, and the app treats the real priorities (cold protection, drainage) as secondary.
Recommended first step: Bring the pot indoors to a bright windowsill now, and check the tray: empty it if there is any water in it.
